title: The Holocaust

cards.h: The murder of six million, planned like paperwork
cards.b:
This lesson is heavy. We tell it plainly because it must be remembered precisely.

Between 1933 and 1945, Nazi Germany and its collaborators persecuted Jews and then murdered about six million of them, two thirds of Europe's Jewish population.
The process began with exclusion, then ghettos, then killing. After the invasion of the USSR in 1941, mobile units called Einsatzgruppen shot over a million Jews, mostly in pits.

At the Wannsee Conference (20 January 1942), officials coordinated the plan to murder all European Jews. Death camps such as Treblinka, Sobibor, Belzec and Auschwitz-Birkenau used gas chambers. About 1.1 million people were murdered at Auschwitz, around 1 million of them Jews.

It needed trains, clerks, police and the silence of many.

The Nazis also murdered Roma and Sinti, disabled people, Soviet prisoners of war, Poles and political prisoners. Jews resisted too, in ghetto uprisings: the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising (April-May 1943) was the largest.

Some non-Jews risked their lives to hide Jews. Israel's Yad Vashem honours them as 'Righteous Among the Nations'.

After the war, the Nuremberg trials (1945-46) tried leading Nazis. Raphael Lemkin, a Polish-Jewish lawyer, coined the word genocide in 1944. The UN adopted the Genocide Convention in 1948.

Holocaust Remembrance Day is observed on 27 January, the day Auschwitz was liberated in 1945.

cards.h: 'The Germans didn't know' and 'Jews didn't fight back'
cards.b: Myth 1: ordinary Germans did not know.Fact: many people saw deportations and knew of killings; how much they knew of the camps is debated, but the persecution was public.Myth 2: Jews went passively. Fact: there was armed resistance in many ghettos and camps, as well as vast spiritual and hidden resistance.

Five things to remember

  1. About six million Jews were murdered.
  2. The process moved from exclusion to killing.
  3. Wannsee coordinated it in January 1942.
  4. Others were murdered too; resistance existed.
  5. Genocide became a legal term.

Think about it

  • Why must we remember specifics?
  • What allows ordinary people to take part in atrocities?
